title: Triage review of c40's CIPS turnover-divide claim (SIED): S, I and D replicate on fresh seeds 4 and 6 to t=8000 (3 and 4 persistent splits, dumbbell pinching, 0 merges); E (the fuel fork) not re-run
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py at its defaults on new seeds 4 and 6 (labkit, 80 frames to t=8000, 192^2). From the smoothed random field (first frame), 3-4 bodies nucleate by t~300 and grow. On seed 6 they elongate and pinch at the waist into two round daughters at t~2800, and again at t~7300 (rerun/seed6/sheet.png). labkit: seed 4, 7 splits, 3 persistent, 0 merges, 10 bodies at t=8000; seed 6, 8 splits, 4 persistent, 0 merges, 12 bodies. Max generation is 1 within t=8000 (c40 reports 2-3 by t~16600-20000). Construction: there is no division rule. The enzyme is made uniformly everywhere at d*e0 and lost at d*e, so bodies grow by influx from the bath (as in Zwicker et al. 2017) and divide by a shape instability. I did not run the fork, so E is not checked.

observations.S: rerun/seed6/sheet.png t=0: smoothed random field over the whole box
observations.I: rerun/seed6/sheet.png: discrete round bodies and rods t=300-8000
observations.D: rerun/seed6/sheet.png: dumbbell pinches at t~2800 and t~7300; FACTS 4 persistent splits, 0 merges; seed 4 3 persistent, 0 merges

verdicts.limitation: Triage only, run to t=8000, so generation 1 is the deepest I saw. The bodies' material comes from a uniform enzyme source in the medium (d*e0 everywhere); E rests on the fuel fork, which I did not repeat.
